## Natural history notes

A small flatid planthopper characterized by a wedge-shaped body, broad tent-like wings, and pale green to yellowish-green coloration with subtle spotting or mottling. In Florida, Flatoidinus punctatus is recorded from multiple parts of the state and is most likely found on shrubs, trees, and ornamental or native vegetation in hammocks, forest edges, gardens, parks, and other warm plant-rich habitats. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing plant tissue and drinking sap, while the waxy nymphs and winged adults serve as prey for spiders, predatory bugs, lacewings, birds, and parasitoid wasps.
